title: Why Forgetting Your Phone Might Help Your Memory
paragraphs: Many people feel lost when they leave their smartphone at home. However, recent research suggests that being without a phone, or at least not using it, may actually help people remember things better.

In 2026, researchers at Binghamton University in the United States published a study in the journal Memory & Cognition about the effect of taking screenshots. The team, which included Sophia Fabrizio and Deanne Westerman, carried out seven experiments, mostly with university students. In the experiments, participants looked at works of art or drawings of everyday objects. They either simply viewed each image or took a screenshot of it with a smartphone, and later their memory was tested.

The results were clear. People remembered the images they had screenshotted much worse than the ones they had only looked at. In one experiment, participants correctly recognized 78% of the art they had viewed, but only 69.5% of the art they had screenshotted. They were also worse at remembering whether they had viewed or screenshotted each image.

Some scientists believe that saving information on a device frees the brain to focus on other tasks. However, the researchers found no clear evidence of this. Even when participants knew in advance that there would be a memory test, the results did not change. According to the researchers, this suggests that the effect may happen "unconsciously and automatically." Their advice is that if you want to remember something important, "your best bet may be to put away your smartphone."
Other research has found similar problems. For example, a study led by Adrian Ward at the University of Texas found that just having a smartphone nearby reduced people's mental performance.

However, the study had some limits. Most participants were young adults tested in a laboratory, and they were not allowed to look at their screenshots later. In daily life, looking at photos again may help people remember.
